blocks.text: The census begins in the wilderness of Sinai, where Israel prepares for the journey ahead. Across Numbers, the principal setting moves from Sinai toward the plains of Moab; Egypt remains the land Israel has left rather than the main location of the narrative.

sections.title: The Census and the Book's Shape

blocks.text: This opening census belongs to the larger geographical movement of Numbers: preparation at Sinai is followed by the journey through Kadesh and the Transjordan, leading to renewed preparation on the plains of Moab. The census here and the later census in Numbers 26 also frame the book's movement from the generation counted at Sinai to the generation prepared for inheritance near Moab. The chapter's repeated tribal totals therefore introduce one of the two generations around which the book is organized.

sections.title: How Should the Numbers Be Understood?

blocks.text: The size of the wilderness population and the relationship between the two census totals have received differing literary and historical interpretations. Because these questions remain disputed, the chapter's figures should be read attentively without presenting any single reconstruction as certain.
